title: RI H7350: Creates additional safety features for AI companion technology that include addressing suicidal ideation, potential physical harm or financial harm to others expressed by a user. It also requires notification the AI companion does not have human emotions.

obligations: Ensure any AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm expressed by a user, possible physical harm to others expressed by a user, and when any of those expressions are made, provide a notification to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))
Beginning July 1, 2027, file annual reports with the office of the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics. (Sec. 6-63-2(b))

Provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three hours for continuing AI companion interactions, stating either verbally or in writing that the user is not communicating with a human. (Sec. 6-63-3)
prohibitions: It is unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless such AI companion contains the required protocol for addressing suicidal ideation, self-harm, physical harm to others, and crisis service notification. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))

key_definitions: AI companion: means a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by: (A) Retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement with the AI companion; (B) Asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion-based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt; and (C) Sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user. AI companion shall not include: (A) Any system used by a business entity solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products provided by such entity, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to its customer service; (B) Any system that is primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance; or (C) Any system used by a business entity solely for internal purposes or employee productivity. (Sec. 6-63-1(1))

Emotional recognition algorithms: means artificial intelligence that detects and interprets human emotional signals in text (using natural language processing and sentiment analysis), audio (using voice emotion AI), video (using facial movement analysis, gait analysis, or physiological signals), or a combination thereof. (Sec. 6-63-1(4))

Generative artificial intelligence: means a class of AI models that are self-supervised and emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content including, but not limited to, images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content. (Sec. 6-63-1(5))

Operator: means any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion. (Sec. 6-63-1(6))
User: means any person who uses an AI companion within the state and who is not an operator or agent or affiliate of the operator of the AI companion. (Sec. 6-63-1(8))

What it does

This law creates safety requirements for AI companion technology. It requires operators to include protocols that address suicidal ideation, self-harm, and physical harm to others expressed by users, and to refer users to crisis services. It also requires operators to notify users that they are not communicating with a human.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of AI companions, defined as any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion (Sec. 6-63-1(6))

Effective date

January 1, 2027 (Sec. 2)

Key definitions

  • AI companion: means a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by: (A) Retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement with the AI companion; (B) Asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion-based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt; and (C) Sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user. AI companion shall not include: (A) Any system used by a business entity solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products provided by such entity, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to its customer service; (B) Any system that is primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance; or (C) Any system used by a business entity solely for internal purposes or employee productivity. (Sec. 6-63-1(1))
  • AI model: means a component of an information system that implements artificial intelligence technology and uses computational, statistical, or machine-learning techniques to produce outputs from a given set of inputs. (Sec. 6-63-1(2))
  • Artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence technology, or AI: means a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments. (Sec. 6-63-1(3))
  • Emotional recognition algorithms: means artificial intelligence that detects and interprets human emotional signals in text (using natural language processing and sentiment analysis), audio (using voice emotion AI), video (using facial movement analysis, gait analysis, or physiological signals), or a combination thereof. (Sec. 6-63-1(4))
  • Generative artificial intelligence: means a class of AI models that are self-supervised and emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content including, but not limited to, images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content. (Sec. 6-63-1(5))
  • Operator: means any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion. (Sec. 6-63-1(6))
  • Person: means any natural person. (Sec. 6-63-1(7))
  • User: means any person who uses an AI companion within the state and who is not an operator or agent or affiliate of the operator of the AI companion. (Sec. 6-63-1(8))

Obligations

  • Ensure any AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm expressed by a user, possible physical harm to others expressed by a user, and when any of those expressions are made, provide a notification to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, file annual reports with the office of the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics. (Sec. 6-63-2(b))
  • Provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three hours for continuing AI companion interactions, stating either verbally or in writing that the user is not communicating with a human. (Sec. 6-63-3)

Prohibitions

  • It is unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless such AI companion contains the required protocol for addressing suicidal ideation, self-harm, physical harm to others, and crisis service notification. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))

Penalties and enforcement

Enforcement is by the attorney general, who may investigate, sue, and seek injunctions against noncompliant AI companion operators. Violations may result in civil penalties up to fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) per day, with fines directed to suicide prevention programs. The text does not state a private right of action. (Sec. 6-63-4(a), (b))

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying an AI companion must implement a safety protocol that detects expressions of suicidal ideation, self-harm, or physical harm to others and refers the user to crisis services. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))
  • The organisation must provide a clear and conspicuous notice at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours that the user is not communicating with a human. (Sec. 6-63-3)
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, the organisation must file annual reports with the attorney general on safety protocol activations and related metrics. (Sec. 6-63-2(b))
  • Noncompliance can lead to attorney general enforcement, injunctions, and civil penalties up to $15,000 per day. (Sec. 6-63-4)

Notable exemptions

  • The definition of AI companion excludes systems used by a business entity solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to its customer service. (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(A))
  • The definition excludes systems primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance. (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(B))
  • The definition excludes systems used by a business entity solely for internal purposes or employee productivity. (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(C))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product meets the definition of AI companion under Sec. 6-63-1(1), including the exclusions.
  • Implement a protocol that detects expressions of suicidal ideation, self-harm, or physical harm to others and provides crisis service referrals as soon as detected. (Sec. 6-63-2(a))
  • Implement a clear and conspicuous notification at the beginning of each interaction and at least every three hours that the user is not communicating with a human. (Sec. 6-63-3)
  • Establish internal processes to track safety protocol activations and related metrics for annual reporting. (Sec. 6-63-2(b))
  • File annual reports with the attorney general beginning July 1, 2027. (Sec. 6-63-2(b))
  • Monitor compliance to avoid attorney general enforcement and civil penalties. (Sec. 6-63-4)
